# repository: # repository  GitHub owner/name allowed to request publication.
# packages    comma-separated shell globs; every .deb in a release must match.
# codenames   comma-separated codenames this producer may publish to; also the
#             default when a request names none.
# attested    no, or WORKFLOW@REF: every .deb must carry a GitHub
#             build-provenance attestation (gh attestation verify) from that
#             workflow file in this repository's .github/workflows. The
#             --signer-workflow argument pins the workflow, and the ref pins
#             the tag pattern or the branch: refs/tags/PATTERN is a shell glob
#             the release tag must match, and the attestation must name
#             refs/tags/<that tag>; refs/heads/BRANCH is an exact branch name,
#             and the release tag can be any value (ADR-0004). `yes` is not a
#             valid value.
# notify      comma-separated repositories sent a `build` dispatch after a
#             successful publish, or - for none.
# component   main or image: the one component this producer's packages go to
#             (core ADR-0059). Every codename it lists must publish that
#             component. image is for builds that replace a Debian package of
#             the same name, or depend on such a build. Changing a producer's
#             component needs the move workflow (move.yml) right after the
#             merge: until it runs, the producer's publications fail closed.
# keep        retention: an integer N from 1 to 999 keeps only the newest N
#             versions of each of the producer's packages (per architecture),
#             and the publication that adds newer ones withdraws the rest from
#             the index in the same run (core ADR-0067). - means no limit. A
#             publication that would withdraw one of its own packages at once
#             is refused. Pool files stay: a pruned version comes back through
#             a rollback, or a republication while it is within the newest N.
#             Every row here has 7 columns (tests/check-config.sh).
# Add a producer only after confirming the package names it ships.
frostyard/updex
# incus builds Debian 13 and Debian 14 in separate jobs and releases each
# build on its own (core Plan 0009 Phase 6). The Debian 14 versions carry
# ~deb14 (1:7.6-debian14-202611131200~deb14), so they route to forky only.
# The Debian 13 versions (1:7.6-debian13-202611131200) carry -debian13-,
# which is not a ~debNN marker: an unmarked version goes to every target, so
# each incus request names its codename (trixie or forky), and a manual
# publish of an incus trixie release must name trixie too.
# It releases from pushes to stable: builds-docker.yml attests and creates
# the release only on refs/heads/stable, so its policy names that branch
# (ADR-0004; Brian, T733a).
# image (core ADR-0059 step 5): Debian 13 ships incus, incus-base,
# incus-client and incus-extra (trixie-security), and the 1: epoch makes these
# builds replace them; incus-ui-canonical goes with them, one producer.
frostyard/incus

frostyard/chairlift
# bootc (Rust) and libostree-1-1 (C) link the libraries of the codename they
# are built in, so each release holds a Debian 13 build carrying ~deb13 and a
# Debian 14 build carrying ~deb14, with one build stamp (core Plan 0009
# Phase 6). The ~deb14 libostree-1-1 must sort above forky's own
# (2026.6-1 on 2026-11-13): a build of the same or a newer ostree does
# (2026.6-frostyard...~deb14 > 2026.6-1). Exact names, not libostree-*, keep
# it from shadowing Debian's other libostree packages.
# It releases from manual workflow_dispatch runs of build.yml on main, so its
# policy names refs/heads/main.
# image (core ADR-0059 step 5): this libostree-1-1 replaces Debian's, and
# bootc links against it.
frostyard/bootc-debian
# The packages of snosi's moonlight and voxtype sysexts (core ADR-0066). The
# ten other omarchy-apps names left the build with snosi's flurry desktop; a

# refs/heads/main. Two versions stay installable: the publication that adds a

frostyard/omarchy-apps
